messages:
maya: heads up — onboarding quickstart README has curl codeblocks with hard linebreaks (\
) that break when copied into PowerShell.

liam: ah yeah saw that. Example?

maya: root snippet:

```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-raw '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

maya: When pasted into PS it spits error about backslash. People copy and remove backslashes incorrectly and miss escaping.

sam: Oof. We should provide both single-line and powershell-friendly examples.

julia: Also the README uses $REDWOOD_KEY which confuses Windows users. Maybe add env var guidance: `setx /M REDWOOD_KEY "..."` for PowerShell and `export REDWOOD_KEY=...` for bash?

sam: Proposed fix: add a one-line curl + a PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod snippet + a note about quoting.

liam: +1. Also add a copy button? but that's more infra. For now PR to README in docs repo.

maya: I'll open PR with the patches — add the PS snippet and replace the line-continuation style with either explicit one-liners and a continuation note.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/312 (draft)

docsonline-bot: Checklist: linkvalidator passed, markdownlint flagged long lines >120, CI docs build ok.

julia: assign to maya for docs changes, @sam can review the snippets for accuracy.

sam: can do review today.

liam: can we also add a tiny note in quickstart that tokens are billed per generated token, not per request? unrelated but requested by SOC.

maya: added that in the draft.

sam: LGTM on plan. Thanks!

julia: thanks — will add a small test: paste snippet into PowerShell -> fails -> confirm fixed after PR.

maya: closing loop once CI passes. :thumbsup:
